entity.description: A user's crypto device (one browser's store), deviceId unique within the user as in Matrix. Its public identity keys (curve25519Key, ed25519Key) and the signed device_keys object as the device uploaded it (deviceKeysJson), which is answered as it is so others can check its signature; the keys cannot change once set. listRevision goes up and listChangedDate is set at each change others should see (keys set, renamed, revoked): a sync answers the users whose devices changed. lastToDevicePos is the stream position of the newest to-device message queued to it (each one queued takes the next). A revoked device (revokedDate) gets no new messages or keys and is left out of queries; it cannot be used again. verifiedDate is what the user's other device said of it (a later C7 pass): trust is held by clients, and this flag establishes none.

field.name: userAgent
field.description: Of the request that made the device, to tell devices apart in My devices

field.name: storeKey
field.description: Legacy: the random passphrase a device made before the store key was derived (get#ChatDeviceStoreKey answers it as legacyStoreKey) encrypted its browser store with. The browser moves that store's keys to a new device under the derived key and revokes this one, which clears it; nothing writes it any more. The field goes once no device holds one.

field.name: storeRevision
field.description: The revision the device's store key is derived from (derive#ChatStoreKey: userId|deviceId|revision under chat_store_key_secret); a revoke bumps it.

entity.description: A device's signed one-time key (isFallback N) or fallback key (Y), keyId as Matrix names it (signed_curve25519:AAAAHg), keyJson the signed key object as uploaded. A one-time key is handed out once: the claim locks the device's row, takes the oldest unclaimed key and sets claimedDate, so two claims at once never get the same key; a claimed one-time key is deleted by the cleanup job. A fallback key is handed out when no one-time key is left and stays (claimedDate marks it used); an upload of a new one replaces it.

A to-device message queued to one device (userId, deviceId) at its stream position (streamPos, the device's lastToDevicePos when it was queued, so a device reads its messages in the order they were queued). Kept until the device acknowledges it: a sync from a position deletes everything up to it. contentJson is the event content as the sending browser gave it (Olm ciphertext for an encrypted event); the server does not read it. txnId is the sender's transaction, so a send retried while its first copy is still queued is not queued again.

A user's cross-signing key of one usage (keyUsage: master, self_signing, user_signing), as uploaded (keyJson, the Matrix CrossSigningKey object) with its single ed25519 public key (publicKey, unpadded base64). The master key is the user's identity: a different one replaces it only on the user's explicit reset (upload#CrossSigningKeys reset), which deletes the old keys and every signature by or over them. The private keys stay in the browser (and its secret storage).

A signature a user uploaded (upload#KeySignatures) over a device (targetKeyId a deviceId) or a cross-signing key (targetKeyId its public key) of targetUserId, by the signer's key signerKeyId ("ed25519:<public key or deviceId>"). Merged into the signed objects key queries answer: a user's signatures over their own keys to everyone in reach, another's only to the signer. The server does not check the signature (the clients do).

A version of a user's server-side key backup (Matrix room_keys, m.megolm_backup.v1.curve25519-aes-sha2): versions are "1", "2", ... per user and never reused; the current one is the latest not deleted. algorithm and authDataJson (auth_data: the backup's public key and its signatures) are as the browser gave them. etag goes up at each change of its keys. A deleted version (deletedDate) has no sessions left.

One backed-up Megolm session of a backup version: roomId (the Matrix room ID the browser names) and sessionId as given, the KeyBackupData fields (firstMessageIndex, forwardedCount, isVerified) by which a better copy replaces it, and sessionDataJson, the session_data encrypted to the backup's key (opaque to the server).

field.name: verifiedDevicesOnly
field.description: Y: an encrypted room whose members' browsers share its keys only with verified or cross-signed devices (set by a moderator: set#RoomVerifiedDevicesOnly). Each user may also turn this on for all their encrypted rooms (the preference CHAT_VERIFIED_DEVICES_ONLY). The browsers apply it; the server only keeps it.
